title: Iskandar Zu al-Karnayn and the Peaceful Folk

full_text:
Iskandar Zu al-Karnayn—the great Alexander who held dominion over the East and the West—marched his victorious armies through the farthest borders of the world. One day, he arrived at a tranquil and secluded valley where a community of people lived in extraordinary harmony.

Entering their town, Iskandar was astonished to observe three strange customs: the people had no locks or bolts upon their doors; they had neither magistrates, jails, nor judges; and before the entrance of every house, a freshly dug grave lay open in the garden!

Iskandar summoned the elders of the town and asked: 'What manner of people are you? Why do you use neither locks nor guards?'

The chief elder smiled serenely: 'O King, none of us steals, because none of us hoards more than his daily bread; and what we have, we share freely with the hungry. When all have enough, who needs an iron lock?'

Iskandar asked: 'And why have you no judges or tribunals?'

The elder replied: 'We have no judges because whenever a dispute arises, both parties search for the path of equity rather than victory; each puts his brother’s right before his own, so justice settles before wrath can ignite.'

Iskandar asked: 'And why have you dug graves before your doorsteps?'

The elder led the monarch to the garden and said: 'We dig our graves so that whenever we step across our thresholds, we remember that we are travelers who possess this earth only for a passing hour. Remembering our mortality, pride withers, greed dies, and our hands remain clean of our brother’s blood.'

Iskandar Zu al-Karnayn took off his royal crown of gold, bowed before the elder, and confessed: 'For thirty years I have conquered empires with the sword, but today I have met a people who have conquered the human heart with wisdom!'
moral: True peace and prosperity flourish where justice rules without greed and men live in harmony with mortality.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "Iskandar Zu al-Karnayn"?

Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
